caption: Three cloud case studies with cloud-workload-to-endpoint ratios of 0.8:1, 4:1 and 36:1 and matching ARR uplift of ~300%, ~50% and ~3,500%: the earliest quantification of why a cloud sensor sale is worth a multiple of an endpoint sale.
source_deck: 2020-10-15 · Investor Product Briefing: Securing the Cloud

caption: Retail customer landed on one module (Intel) in FY15 and reached seven modules and $3m ARR by FY21, 3,500%+ ARR expansion and 400%+ sensor expansion, with each step labelled by module added and sensor growth.

Quarterly gross and net dollar retention from Q1 FY18 to Q4 FY21: gross retention climbed from 94% to 98%, net retention peaked at 147% in Q4 FY19 and settled at 125%. Neither series appears quarterly in the filings.
FY17-FY21 actual subscription gross margin and S&M/R&D/G&A ratios laid against the IPO target model and the then-current FY25 target, showing S&M falling from 101% of revenue to 40% in four years.

Subscription ARR earned per $1 of initial incident-response or proactive services spend: $3.73 in FY20, $5.51 in FY21, $5.71 in FY22. Puts a number on the claim that the loss-making services unit is a subscription lead generator.
Enterprise penetration at Jan 31, 2022: 65 of the Fortune 100, 254 of the Fortune 500, 15 of the top 20 US banks and 526 of the Global 2000, each with its year-over-year gain.
Module adoption on the 4+/5+/6+ basis for FY18-FY22, the series later re-based to 5+/6+/7+ and then to 6+/7+/8+; the only place the older cut is charted through FY22.
Full-platform opportunity inside the existing base: $2.8bn against $1.1bn ARR at FY21 and $7.0bn against $1.7bn at FY22. The first point in a whitespace series restated at every briefing since.

Modeling guidance that stock compensation would fall to the mid-teens as a percentage of revenue by FY26 and capex would normalise to 5-8% from FY24, a testable forecast against H1 FY2027 SBC of $674.6m.
IDC modern-endpoint share with vendors named: CrowdStrike 17.7% at #1, other next-gen vendors 7.4% combined (VMware 4.6%, SentinelOne 2.8%), legacy signature vendors 46.7% of which Microsoft 16.4%.
The arithmetic behind the $5bn+ ARR by FY26 goal: three times FY23 net new ARR, with FY24 assumed flat and growth resuming in FY25. Ending ARR reached $5.25bn at Jan 31, 2026.
Minimum ARR to rank as a top-25, top-100 or top-400 account: $7.2m, $2.9m and $1.1m at FY23 against $1.1m, $298k and $60k at FY18, showing how fast the top of the account base scaled.
Ending ARR split across three customer-size bands for FY18, FY22 and FY23: $1,167m from customers above $1m ARR, $975m from $100k-$1m and $417m below $100k. No filing discloses this split.
Twenty-four quarters of gross and net retention through Q4 FY23, extending the FY21 chart: gross retention held at 97-98% while net retention slid from 147% to 125%.
Free-cash-flow margin expectations of 30% in FY24 and FY25, 30-32% in FY26 and 32%+ thereafter. FY2026 free cash flow margin came in at 26%.

The Next-Gen SIEM thesis in one page: LogScale ARR from $5.5m at launch in 1Q22 to about $100m by 2Q24, Falcon already producing ~85% of the data sitting in third-party SIEMs, and a $16bn CY28 opportunity.
Charlotte AI list pricing of $20 per endpoint per year with a query allocation plus paid query packs, one of very few published per-module price points anywhere in the disclosure record.
Customer counts against named rivals: CrowdStrike above 23,000 versus Palo Alto 80,000, Box 100,000, Salesforce 150,000, Atlassian 260,000, Trend Micro 500,000, VMware 500,000 and Fortinet 680,000.
Penetration of the three growth lines inside the installed base at 2Q24: 34% of customers on cloud security, 9% on identity, 3% on LogScale. The denominator for the cross-sell case.
Financial-services account from FY15 to FY24: landed on two modules, reached nine modules and $5m ARR, about 400% total ARR expansion, with each year split between modules added and sensor growth.
The FY29 target model as first set: 82-85% subscription gross margin, 28-32% operating margin and 34-38% free cash flow margin, with the basis-point change from the prior target on every line.

Total account value of Falcon Flex customers moving from above $185m in 4Q24 to above $500m in 1Q25 and above $700m in 2Q25, alongside the licensing terms (1-5 years, swappable modules, sized to demand).

A post-incident customer commitment package priced out: a semiconductor customer went from $0.6m to $1.1m ARR on a $3.0m 36-month contract, of which the customer funded $2.0m and CrowdStrike invested $0.6m.
Matrix mapping each commitment-package incentive (module adds, professional services, payment terms, term elongation and discounting) to its effect on ARR, revenue, gross margin and cash.
Eight years of module adoption on the 5+/6+/7+ basis, FY18 to 2Q25, ending at 65%/45%/29%. The 5+ metric was retired after Q4 FY2025, so this is the longest published run of the series.
A Fortune 500 conglomerate through two Flex cycles: $5m ARR on seven modules, then $24m on ten, then $57m on fourteen, with total contract value moving $14m to $103m to $246m.
CrowdStrike Financial Services one year after launch: $230m of cumulative loan value, over half the portfolio tied to Flex deals and 95% funding new logos or platform expansion.

The FY29 target model reaffirmed unchanged two years after it was set: 82-85% subscription gross margin, 28-32% operating margin, 34-38% free cash flow margin, against 22% non-GAAP operating margin in FY2026.
The ARR ladder extended: $4.7bn at 2Q26, $10bn by FY31 from cloud, identity and SIEM, then $20bn by FY36 at a 15% CAGR from agentic SOC and agentic-everywhere products still unbuilt.
Illustrative FY31 ARR by product line against CY30 market size: cloud $2.5-3.0bn of $49bn, identity $1.0-1.5bn of $19bn, next-gen SIEM $1.5-2.0bn of $48bn, an implied share of 3-6%.
Install-base whitespace at 2Q26: $25.2bn of total opportunity against $4.7bn of ARR. The ratio has compressed from 6.8x at 2Q24 as ARR grew faster than the module set it is measured against.

The Flex expansion ladder quantified: 40%+ average ARR uplift converting from standard to Flex, 25% on the first re-Flex and 53% for accounts that re-Flexed twice or more, with 2,900+ Flex and 630+ re-Flex customers.
